bib.title: MuSiQue: Multihop Questions via Single-hop Question Composition

question: Can a multihop QA dataset be built so that, by construction, it requires connected multihop reasoning and cannot be solved by shortcuts?
hypothesis: Composing carefully filtered single-hop questions bottom-up yields a harder, less cheatable multihop dataset than crowdsourced or rule-composed ones.
contributions: A bottom-up dataset construction pipeline composing connected single-hop questions (MuSiQue condition, Eqn 2).
MuSiQue-Ans (~25K 2-4 hop questions) and MuSiQue-Full (~50K, adds unanswerable contrast questions), with empirical analysis against HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA.

method.summary: Single-hop questions from five Wikipedia-based datasets are filtered, paired through bridge entities, disconnection-filtered with Longformer models, composed into 2-4 hop DAGs, split to minimise train-test leakage, given 20-paragraph contexts with positive distractors, and phrased by MTurk workers. Models (Longformer, RoBERTa, BART, T5 variants) are trained on 20K-instance sets and compared with human scores.
method.task: multihop reading comprehension QA (answer + supporting paragraph identification, plus answerability in Full)

datasets.name: MuSiQue-Ans
datasets.size: 24,814 questions (train 19,938; dev 2,417; test 2,459); by hops, train 14376/4387/1175 for 2/3/4-hop
datasets.split: train/dev/test with minimal overlap of single-hop questions, answers, paragraphs
datasets.source: SQuAD, Natural Questions, MLQA (en-en), T-REx, Zero Shot RE
datasets.preprocessing: remove questions no one of five QA models answers with F1>0; drop contexts <20 or >300 words; 20 paragraphs per question

datasets.name: MuSiQue-Full
datasets.source: adds one unanswerable twin per question
datasets.preprocessing: one sampled single-hop answer removed from all context paragraphs

models.name: Step Execution EX(EE)/EX(SA)
models.architecture: BART-large decomposer + single-hop executor (EE or SA)

models.name: RNN baseline
models.architecture: re-implementation of Yang et al. 2018 model

models.name: Artifact models (Q-only, C-only, 1-Para)
models.architecture: BART-large (Q-only); Longformer-Large EE with empty Q (C-only); SA with K=1 (1-Para)

training.objective: selector cross-entropy relevance classification; span answer/support prediction per Beltagy et al. 2020; binary answerability via CLS
training.seeds: disconnection filter: two Longformer-Large seeds per 5-fold split; eval seeds not stated

other.note: no optimizer or hyperparameter table in the paper

inference.samples: single run per model; not stated
inference.retrieval: BM25 via Elasticsearch for distractors at construction; models read the given 20 paragraphs

metrics.name: An (answer F1)
metrics.definition: token-overlap F1 per Yang et al. 2018

metrics.name: An+Sf / Sp+Sf
metrics.definition: for answerable/unanswerable pairs, 0 if sufficiency is mispredicted on either, else the An (Sp) score of the answerable instance; averaged over pairs

metrics.name: DiRe score
metrics.definition: extent a dataset can be cheated by disconnected reasoning (Trivedi et al. 2020), computed with SA

eval.protocol: validation for HQ/2W and ablations, test for Table 5; human scores from 125 sampled questions per dataset with 3 MTurk annotations, 7 of 15 workers qualified

limits: Evaluation covers only fine-tuned Longformer/BART/T5-era models; no LLM prompting results (dated for current RL/RAG use).
Reading-comprehension setting with 20 given paragraphs; open-domain extension is left to future work.
Disconnection filter enforced only on head questions' first condition and tail via filter; filter uses transformer models, which could bias difficulty (RNN baseline checks this).
Training hyperparameters, optimizer, hardware and seeds are not reported.
Human performance estimated from 125 questions per dataset.
